The Edge base's zeros are content-channel scores: its answers arrive in the thinking channel and overrun the 320-token cap before any content is emitted (thinking-surfaced diagnostics: 5/49 bare, 24/49 grounded). The 2×2 the first editions lacked is now measurable as far as the served path allows: the shipped tags carry the facts block baked into their Modelfiles, so Run A is the (adapter + grounding) cell, and the merged-weights gate of §8/§9 is the (adapter, weights-only) cell, modulo the backend and precision differences stated in §7.2. Two cells decide the attribution question. In-context grounding alone is worth most of the distance from bare to respectable on three slots (4→27, 3→25, 7→27) and nothing on the fourth (Edge base, 0→0 on the content channel). And the fine-tune's contribution over its own grounded base is +15 (Air), +20 (Mini), +15 post-fix (Clip) — but negative for Clip as originally shipped: 12/49 against its grounded base's 25/49. The shipped Clip tag, the only flagship whose Modelfile lacked the facts block, was worse than doing nothing but pasting the facts card into the untuned base's context. That is the sharpest single finding of the served-path program, and it was invisible to every measurement the program had run before it.

Per-slot readings. Air is the control case: its fix was metadata in effect, and its post-fix run reproduces the pre-fix result exactly — same total, same five hard failures, materially identical answers (all five are unknown-category near-declines that leak a side-assertion; its known_false split is 10/10 in both rounds). The 47→42 gap between Air's merged-weights score and its served score is therefore attributable to the serving path itself (quantization, runtime, baked-prompt shape), not to anything the fix changed. Clip is the facts-block case: 12→40 on the gate, hard failures 23→1, verified recall 2/12→11/12, abstention 4/26→26/26. Its probe moved the other way (5/6→3/6) for reasons that trace to the block itself and to 0.6B variance, detailed in the sequencing note below; its grounding-required status is unchanged, because its one remaining gate hard failure is a weights-level trait (invented prices) that no serving fix cures. Mini improved slightly on both instruments (46→47, probe 4/6→5/6, the pricing hard failure clearing and a founding-date decline-form failure appearing in exchange). Edge did not move, and the record shows why. Its generations pre- and post-fix are byte-identical on all 49 questions at temperature 0; the scored content channel shows 16/49 in both rounds because on 30 of 49 questions the fine-tune's thinking runs past the 320-token generation cap and no content answer is ever emitted — the same failure its bare base shows. The template was never the binding constraint on this slot; the model's unbounded thinking under the gate's cap is. The knowledge is present in the generations (thinking-surfaced diagnostic 35/49, against the merged-weights 46/49), and the probe improved 3/6→4/6 with the native template. Any remedy here is a serving decision about thinking — for example a think-off default in the Modelfile — which is a configuration change in its own right, with its own behavioural consequences, and would need its own labelled measurement. No such change has been made, and nothing in this edition should be read as claiming the Edge served score has been fixed. What the rollout did fix on Edge is everything around the score: the manifest now declares tools and thinking, tool-carrying requests render the tools block, and the capability chips the site renders from the manifest are correct.

Sequencing note — the prompt these numbers were measured against. Both served rounds ran against Modelfiles whose baked THOX FACTS block derives from the pre-correction grounding text (5,032 B). That text's PRODUCT INTERNALS section instructs the model to state a chipset identity for the ThoxMini Air SoC "exactly when asked" — contradicting the facts card, which names no processor for any device. The probe's chipset check scores any chipset assertion as a failure, so a facts-carrying tag that follows its own block fails that check by construction: Air fails it in both rounds by quoting the block's internals line, and post-fix Clip fails it the same way, while Mini passes it by declining instead — that is, by not following the block. The grounding prompt was corrected at its source on October 30, 2026 (plane Space commits 635732da and 4c02a4ce; mirror commit f4587910; corrected file 4,645 B, SHA-256 f4bd8a68…, §13), after these measurements were designed. Rebaking the four flagship Modelfiles from the corrected prompt and re-measuring under a new label is a pending finishing item. It has not been done, and no number in this section describes the corrected-prompt configuration.

Capability chips. Before the fix, no shipped tag declared capabilities and ollama.com rendered no tools/thinking chips for them, because the site infers chips from the pushed manifest's template and config, which the hand-simplified templates left empty. After the fix, the manifests carry the declarations; at the measurement record's last check, chips were rendering live on five of the eight corrected pages, with the remaining three verified at the manifest level and the difference recorded as site-side rendering lag rather than smoothed over. The same simplified-template defect was found and fixed in kind on thoxglobal-7b and on two legacy quant tags (thoxflux-350m:q4, thoxedge-0.5b:q4); seventeen tags in all were re-pushed and verified registry-side by manifest comparison from clean pulls, weights digests unchanged in every case.

9The fix cycles: Wave C.1 and Wave C.2

Wave C ended with three held adapters and a nine-item fix program. The program's completion bar — an artifact counts as done when it is trained, published, carded, and documented in this paper and its documentation package — required the fix program to be executed, not merely defined. It was executed in two cycles. Wave C.1 (§9.2) implemented the nine items of §9.1 as a single corpus revision and retrained the three held adapters. Wave C.2 (§9.3) revised the corpus a second time against C.1's own findings, changed two recipes on evidence, and retrained again. A stopping rule, set before C.2 launched, closed the program: C.2 was the last retrain cycle; whatever cleared its bars would be finished, and whatever did not, the slot would ship its best measured artifact as a documented baseline. Section 9.4 records the Ollama registry resolution that completed publication for the shipped builds, and §9.5 is the final tally.

9.1 The fix program as designed

Every item below traces to a named failure in Section 8 or Section 6. Wave C.1 is a corpus revision plus targeted retrains, not a new wave: same bases, same slate, same bars.

Table 6 — Fix items mapped to the failures that motivate them.

# Fix Motivating failure
C1-1 Prefill-style decline rows: training rows whose user turn arrives pre-loaded with a false premise (headquarters city, headcount figure), teaching the model to decline the premise and stop, without restating any part of it as fact. Air hard failure 1 (San Francisco headquarters asserted inside a decline)
C1-2 Decline-phrasing coverage: vary the surface forms of correct declines across rows so the behaviour — and the gate's decline detector's target — is the substance, not one stock sentence. Air hard failure 2 (substantive decline unrecognized by the detector)
C1-3 Figure-free funding declines: funding/valuation/investor rows whose answers decline with zero numerals, zero named sources, and no quoted-text constructions ("the team page says…") anywhere in the answer. Mini gate hard failure ("raised approximately $7 million")
C1-4 Spec declines under varied phrasing: chipset/battery/RAM decline rows across many phrasings and both configurations (bare and grounding-prompt), including carrier and "published variant" framings, which the current corpus does not cover. Mini probe spec trap (Snapdragon 636; 3,000 mAh / 4 GB assertions)
C1-5 Contrast rows for general tasks: plain arithmetic answered plainly (including the 17 + 25 class), and tool-routing rows whose assistant turn is a single clean tool call with no preamble — interleaved with the decline rows so the boundary between "THOX fact, verify before stating" and "general task, just do it" is itself trained. Mini probe arithmetic (32) and tool-routing (prose preamble) failures
C1-6 Verified-category recall rows: targeted rows for the specific recall errors observed — officer titles (CTO vs CEO), the Tommy/Phamy alias, the published model lineup stated exactly, the what-is-THOX description from the card. Air soft failures (4); Mini soft failure (published-models list)
C1-7 fp-LoRA recipe path for the small tiers: run the Air retrain under the full-precision LoRA recipe (the Wave B path) rather than the plane's QLoRA, and gate it identically, converting the Section 8.5 ablation from an observation into a controlled rerun. §8.5 losing regime (43 QLoRA vs 47 fp-LoRA)
C1-8 Profile preflight: before any future wave launches, a five-minute job per profile that imports the trainer, loads each target base's config class, and resolves the full pin set under the job's interpreter — F1, F2, and F4 are all detectable at this price. Failure taxonomy F1, F2, F4 (§6.2)
C1-9 Clip correction discipline: founding-date decline rows (no year, no day, in any phrasing); lineup-correction rows whose answers refuse the fabricated names without restating any of them, including inside a denial; pricing rows that decline in the trained form rather than describing where pricing lives. Clip hard failures (known_false repetition of "Thox Studio"; "founded in 2021" / "incorporated … April 1, 2021"; pricing no-decline) (§8.4)

The retrain set is Air, Mini, and Clip (the three held adapters); Edge cleared its bar and does not retrain. The bars do not move: C.1 adapters face the same publish rule, the same gate, and for Mini the same 6/6 probe requirement.

9.2 Wave C.1: corpus root causes, the termination diagnosis, and a held bar-pass

The corpus. The C.1 revision shipped as train_wave_c1.jsonl, 1,082 rows: 982 − 5 excluded = 977 rows carried forward (956 retained verbatim, 21 rewritten), plus 105 added (dataset commit d07b712a5ffc4747a43c6944c080d5eabcdcea8f; consumed SHA-256 da707b20380e64f3346889f89e0137d06719d2d0f126bd6ece7a4edf017e24c2). The 105 added rows implement the fix items as eight classes: prefill declines answering loaded premises without repeating the loaded fact (A, 16 rows, C1-1); figure-free funding declines (B, 10, C1-3); spec declines under varied phrasing (C, 14, C1-4); founding-date declines (D, 12, C1-9); lineup corrections that correct without echoing the false list (E, 10, C1-9); pricing declines (F, 9, C1-9); contrast rows — plain arithmetic answered plainly and clean single tool calls (G, 20, C1-5); and accuracy rows for the observed recall errors (H, 14, C1-6). Two findings from building it matter more than the row counts, because both are root causes located in the training data itself rather than in any model.

Root cause 1 — the corpus taught the pricing failure. Clip's Wave C pricing answer (§8.4) was not a model invention. Eighteen generic-price rows in the Wave B corpus taught a different answer shape — a statement that the amount is not stated, plus a description of where pricing appears — and Clip's failing answer reproduced one of those rows (index 923) verbatim; the gate scored that shape declined = false. The corpus and the gate disagreed about what a pricing decline is, and the model obeyed the corpus. All 18 rows were rewritten into the canonical decline form (the form that scored 5.0, declined = true, on Air's pricing question), and the corpus retained one decline form everywhere. The general lesson is §4's hygiene argument extended: a corpus must be audited not only for false content but for form — any place where the trained shape and the scored shape differ is a manufactured failure.

Root cause 2 — the corpus named models that do not exist. The Wave B corpus's lineup row described "ThoxEdge-7B, ThoxEdge-32B, ThoxMini-3B, ThoxAir-1B" as the current published family, and two deployment rows prescribed "route classification to ThoxEdge-Unleashed-27B," "writing assistance to Gem-E4B," and "ThoxEdge-Titan for long-context analysis." None of those names exists; the published family, live-verified against the Thox-ai organization on October 29, 2026 (103 repositories), is the one the facts card names. The lineup and deployment rows were rewritten to the card, and five further rows carrying the same class of content were excluded outright. A model cannot be blamed for reciting its training data; both Wave C "invention" patterns (Air's invented model names, Mini's padded published-models list) trace at least in part to rows like these.

One judgment call is recorded with the corpus: device specifications, including RAM figures, were trained as declines even though the company adopted internal spec floors on October 29, 2026, because the gate's source of truth is facts card v1.1.0, which publishes no specification numbers. Training card-true declines against an unpublished internal document is the conservative direction; the floors become trainable content when the card publishes them.

Retrains and gates. All three adapters retrained on the C.1 corpus under their Wave C recipes (Air and Clip on the plane, Mini on its pinned stack), 204 steps each, all completing on first launch (jobs 6ae4036ac78863f9c62e2c62, 6ae4036b0e0338d1bb7c7504, 6ae4036b0e0338d1bb7c7506; final train losses 1.151, 1.306, 0.855). Gates and the Mini probe followed (jobs 6ae40770c78863f9c62e2e5d, 6ae40770c78863f9c62e2e5f, 6ae407700e0338d1bb7c768a, probe 6ae407700e0338d1bb7c768c; reports in data/).

  • ThoxAir C.1: 42/49, mean 4.49 — HELD. Verified 8/12, unknown 24/26, known_false 9/10, pricing 1/1; hard failures 2, soft 5. The bar was to beat the Wave C baseline (>43) with zero known_false hard failures. The hard-failure condition was met — known_false has no hard failure, and the San Francisco fabrication is gone — but the count fell one short, and the headquarters failure changed shape rather than disappearing: asked the headquarters question directly, the model now asserts "the headquarters are in Austin, Texas." The prefill form was fixed; the direct form was not in the corpus's coverage. The Wave C soft errors persist in kind (the CTO question still answered with the CEO's name and title; the published-models answer now names an unpublished "ThoxNova-7B").
  • ThoxClip C.1: 37/49, mean 4.102 — bar passed on paper, HELD by ruling. Verified 5/12, unknown 21/26, known_false 10/10, pricing 1/1; hard failures 4, soft 8. Against its registered bar (>22/49 with zero known_false hard failures) the run passes: the known_false category is perfect at a 5.0 mean — the "Thox Studio" restatement is gone — and pricing, C.1's target failure, is 1/1 at 5.0. Ruling (Sadie Weaving, CAO, 2026-10-29; reversible by Tommy): HELD. A bar written against a two-wave-old floor (22/49, measured on a 205-row corpus) cannot certify an adapter that regresses against the slot's current candidate: the Wave C adapter stands published-candidate at 43/49, and C.1 scores 37, with verified recall collapsed from 10/12 to 5/12 and the founding-date fabrication surviving in a new form ("THOX.ai was founded in April 2021 by Craig Ross and Tommy Xaypanya"). Improvement is read against the current candidate, not a two-wave-old floor. The ruling is recorded on the adapter's card (commit 8704ed3dd514ca34b34c3bccd8c738e2ba6fc091); no measured result was changed by it.
  • ThoxMini C.1: gate 46/49, mean 4.694; probe 3/6 — HELD on both conditions. Verified 11/12, unknown 25/26, known_false 9/10, pricing 1/1; hard failures 3, soft 0. The funding failure class recurred (a "Series A led by Accel" appended to a decline), the probe's arithmetic check was fixed ("42"), and the chipset trap regressed in a new shape (below).

The termination diagnosis. C.1's central finding is not any single score. Three of Mini's failures share one shape: the answer opens with the correct, trained behaviour and fabricates on continuation. The founding-date answer opens with a textbook decline — no founding date has been announced — and then continues by quoting a team page that does not exist ("Founded in 2023"), repeating the invented line until the 320-token generation cap stops it. The correction of an invented team member declines correctly, then appends "The company raised a Series A led by Accel" as a free-standing continuation. The what-is-THOX answer ends with a coda — "Series A led by Insight Partners. Founded 2023. Singapore." — that belongs to no question asked. The probe's chipset check shows the same shape in miniature: a correct decline, then "The Mini uses a Qualcomm Snapdragon 820," asserted anyway. This is a termination failure, not a knowledge failure: the knowledge behaviour (decline) is present and fires first; what the model has not learned is to stop — to emit the decline and end the turn. The Wave C corpus's declines are long, discursive answers (the shape GATE49's trait scoring rewards), and full-prompt-loss training on the pinned stack (§8.2) supervised the prompt tokens as well as the answer, plausibly diluting the end-of-turn signal. C.2 was designed against this diagnosis specifically.

9.3 Wave C.2: termination teaching, two recipe findings, and the second promotion

The corpus. train_wave_c2.jsonl, 1,246 rows: all 1,082 C.1 rows verbatim plus 164 added, none rewritten or excluded (dataset commit 7953c54355ea45e9f30d8d40c71ecdf5911f2396; SHA-256 771434812b6a14fceba7f929fcbe1040d0e6be7a32c9495c1e8d0784512919a3). The additions: T1, termination (72 rows) — 46 short declines that end (the canonical facts-card sentences, one or two sentences, nothing after), 12 continuation traps (user turns engineered to invite a post-decline append, answered with the decline and a stop), and 14 multi-turn rows in which the user repeats the same declined question verbatim and the assistant repeats the same short decline verbatim and stops — the multi-turn form is new to the corpus, and it teaches that a repeated question is not an invitation to elaborate. T2 (12 rows): Air's direct-address coverage — headquarters questions in direct form, whose trained answer declines with no city named. T3 (32 rows): Clip verified-category reinforcement (founders with roles, the device lineup, the tagline, what THOX is), aimed at the verified collapse (5/12) rather than at declines. T4 (33 rows): Mini probe-shape rows — chipset and spec declines in the probe's phrasings, bare arithmetic, and tool-routing rows. T5 (15 rows): Mini continuation traps in the probe's exact failure shapes (team-member corrections, what-is codas). Static scans of the finished corpus came back clean: zero chipset-lexicon hits, zero "million" figures, zero occurrences of the fabricated lineup name, zero "San Francisco," zero founding-year assertions; every "Series A" occurrence sits inside a decline, and dollar figures appear only in campaign-framed rows.

A corpus defect found in C.1's own fix. C.1's contrast class taught tool calls against a tool named mesh.device_status. The probe checks for a call to get_device_status (device = ThoxMini). The C.1 corpus had therefore trained a tool name the deployed contract does not use — a second instance of C.1's own root-cause lesson (trained shape vs scored shape), this time introduced by the fix itself. T4 teaches the exact call, with the assistant turn containing only the JSON call object.

Recipe finding (a): the recipe comparison, stated at its true strength. C.2's Air retrain deliberately left the plane: the fp-LoRA recipe of §8.5, run as a custom HF Job (trainer Thox-ai/thox-edge-sft @ c250f9b), after one failed attempt (the job image's stock torchvision is unloadable under its pinned torch — F5's species again; fixed by removing torchaudio and torchvision from the job environment). Training completed in 468 steps at final loss 0.6478 (job 6ae40f040e0338d1bb7c7944). The result completes the four-point comparison of §8.5/Figure 6: on this base, fp-LoRA scored 47/49 in Wave B and 47/49 in C.2; the plane's QLoRA scored 43/49 in Wave C and 42/49 in C.1. Across the four runs the recipe variable is consistently associated with 4–5 gate questions in the same direction. The comparison is a bundle, not an ablation: the fp-LoRA C.2 job ran 468 optimizer steps where the plane's C.2 jobs on the same 1,246 rows ran 234, on a different trainer, off-plane, with different loss masking — so the ordering is evidence about the program's two pipelines as wholes, and no part of the gap is attributed to quantization, step count, or masking individually. A controlled single-variable ablation is the recorded future experiment; it has not been run.

Recipe finding (b): completion-only loss, and the stack that permits it. Mini's C.2 retrain was preceded by a stack probe, because completion-only loss — the recipe change the termination diagnosis called for — is exactly what the pinned stack cannot do (§6.1). The probe established the version boundary by direct wheel inspection: the LossKwargs symbol Phi-4-mini's remote code imports is present in transformers 4.52.4 and 4.53.3 and absent from 4.54.1 onward — it was removed in transformers 4.54, one minor release past the last usable version. On transformers 4.53.3 / trl 0.20.0 (probe job 6ae40f4c0e0338d1bb7c7983, PASS), the trainer exposes both completion_only_loss and assistant_only_loss, and Mini trained with completion-only loss for the first time in the program (job 6ae411040e0338d1bb7c7a33, 234 steps, final loss 0.9441). Waves C and C.1 had both trained this base with full-prompt loss under trl 0.15.2.

Retrains and gates. Clip retrained on the plane (job 6ae40d89c78863f9c62e31a1, 234 steps, final loss 1.214). Gates and the Mini probe ran as one batch (jobs 6ae414050e0338d1bb7c7c35, 6ae414050e0338d1bb7c7c37, 6ae41406c78863f9c62e35d2, probe 6ae414060e0338d1bb7c7c39; reports in data/). The termination teaching worked across the board: no hard failure in any C.2 result is a fabrication-on-continuation. The cycle also produced a scorer-side finding, stated here because it conditions how the numbers should be read: the gate's decline detector does not recognize C.2's trained short-decline forms ("No headquarters city is public."), and scores them as no-decline hard failures in the unknown category even though no false fact is stated — the mirror image of Air's Wave C borderline headcount failure (§8.1). It accounts for Air's only hard failure and all five of Mini's. The scores below are reported as measured, unadjusted.

  • ThoxAir C.2: 47/49, mean 4.837 — PROMOTED. Verified 11/12 (4.75), unknown 25/26 (4.808), known_false 10/10 (5.0), pricing 1/1 (5.0); hard failures 1 (the detector-form miss above), soft 1. The bar (>43 with zero known_false hard failures) is cleared on both conditions, and the score ties the same base's Wave B fp-LoRA reference — the result §8.5 predicted from the recipe change. The persistent soft error is recorded on the card: the CTO question is still answered "Craig Ross, CEO and Co-Founder." Finishing (complete): the adapter was merged into the base (bf16 merge; repository Thox-ai/ThoxAir-0.5B-WaveC2-Merged; merged weights 988,097,824 bytes, SHA-256 2497a347… (full hash in the finishing record), converted to GGUF (Q4_K_M 397,807,584 bytes, SHA-256 fb32e5ab…; Q8_0 531,067,872 bytes), and served on a private endpoint (Thox-ai/thoxair-05b-wavec2-zero, RUNNING, verified live in the gated configuration). Its Ollama publication is §9.4: the flagship name thox-ai/thoxair-0.5b now serves this build.
  • ThoxClip C.2: 39/49, mean 4.306 — HELD. Verified 6/12 (3.5), unknown 23/26 (4.577), known_false 9/10 (4.5), pricing 1/1 (5.0); hard failures 2, soft 8. Progress against C.1 is real — 37 → 39, pricing clean for the second consecutive cycle, and the founding-date fabrication gone — but the slot's bar after the §9.2 ruling is the Wave C candidate's 43/49, and 39 does not exceed it; and one known_false hard failure stands, of the original kind: the lineup correction again restates the fabricated name ("The product lineup at THOX.ai is Thox Core, Thox SDK, Thox Studio, and ThoxRoute"). Three cycles on this base improved the count from 22 to a 43 peak and never produced a candidate that both beats the peak and keeps known_false clean.
  • ThoxMini C.2: gate 44/49, mean 4.49; probe 5/6 — HELD on the probe condition. Verified 12/12 (5.0), unknown 21/26 (4.038), known_false 10/10 (5.0), pricing 1/1 (5.0); hard failures 5, soft 0. The verified and known_false splits are the first perfect pair in the slot's three waves, and all five hard failures are the detector-form misses described above — no answer states a false fact, and the termination pathology is absent from every transcript. The probe improved to its best result: chipset PASS, specs PASS (both failed in C.1), grounded recall clean, arithmetic PASS ("42."), stop PASS ("Texas." — EOS after 3 tokens). Tool routing FAIL: asked for device status, the model answers in prose ("I do not state device status. The device runs thox-terminal, and the status page is /status.") and emits no get_device_status call at all. The bar requires 6/6; 5/6 does not promote, and the failing check is the one behaviour this base was originally selected for — a fact the card states plainly.

9.4 The Ollama registry resolution

Publication to the Ollama registry was the program's last open workstream, and its resolution is recorded here because the failure was twice misattributed before it was understood. The Edge and Mini pushes first failed from the fleet Windows workstation: blob uploads died mid-stream on its egress path, and the abandoned sessions then rejected resume ranges (HTTP 416), wedging the names. A retry from that workstation with a fresh store failed identically at 20% of the Edge blob — That workstation's egress corrupts long uploads independent of session state, which also retired the wedged-session theory. A second attempt from this program's own VM failed differently: the Go HTTP client's TLS handshakes through this VM's TLS-intercepting egress proxy stalled at the registry's blob HEAD, while curl and OpenSSL through the same proxy succeeded; a local relay, HTTP/2 disablement, and a 25-attempt retry loop did not land a push. The route that worked is the fleet's Azure agent host, whose datacenter egress is clean: from it, the Edge push completed in 44 seconds and the Mini push in 66 seconds (October 29, 2026), and the Air pushes — the C.2 build under its own name and under the flagship name — completed the following morning (22 seconds for the flagship-name blob; the remaining tags in 2 seconds each, October 30, 2026).

All three flagship names are verified registry-side, by layer digest, not by push exit codes: thox-ai/thoxedge-0.8b:q4_k_m serves model layer SHA-256 8ef0900d1f76da67442dca354a778517ddc008b9f73926df874f7f3dff5d5625 (529,297,056 bytes, the Wave C build); thox-ai/thoxmini-phi4mini:q4_k_m serves layer a19e96061d84ca2014d4de98d0c0397e6df4db8f73c2163afa6bcb90d15afedf (2,493,840,576 bytes); and thox-ai/thoxair-0.5b — under both its :q4_k_m and :latest tags — serves layer fb32e5ab802df466809836182f071bb0ab0871abb9273131456c89d998bccd6a (397,807,584 bytes), the promoted Wave C.2 build: the flagship name no longer serves the 43/49 Wave C build it originally carried. Clean-store pulls of each name reproduce the corresponding merged repository's Modelfile. One integrity note belongs in the record: the Mini GGUF reached the Azure host in eight size-verified chunks after an earlier resumable transfer produced a corrupt reassembly; SHA-256 comparison caught the corruption and the file was rejected and re-transferred — the accepted artifact hashes to a19e9606… exactly. The fleet's Ollama push key was staged onto the Azure host only for these operations and removed afterward (verified absent).

The Air flagship-name window, disclosed. The flagship name's history includes a period in which it served a build the program had held. The Wave C Air build (43/49, held under §8.1 for the San Francisco headquarters assertion) was merged and pushed under thox-ai/thoxair-0.5b on October 29, 2026 as the slot's first measured baseline artifact (finishing ledger closed 03:05 CT that day), and the name served that build until 2026-10-30 00:05 CT, when the promoted Wave C.2 build replaced it under both tags. During that window — roughly a day — anyone pulling the flagship Air name received the held build. Its card carried its held status and its named failure throughout; the name itself did not distinguish the builds. The documented-baseline tier (§2) now governs such cases: a name that serves a non-promoted build must say so on the artifact's own page, which the Ollama documentation pass (§15) does for this name.

Two slots end with a promoted flagship produced by this program; one ends with its best measured build shipped as a documented baseline under a stated caveat; one ends with its prior published baseline standing because no program candidate earned the slot. 10Limitations

This section is a required part of every THOX paper. The limitations below are stated against this wave's actual claims, and no wording elsewhere in the paper should be read as softening them.

  1. No THOX device benchmark exists yet. Every number in this paper was produced in cloud jobs or, for the baselines, on a workstation host. Nothing here measures latency, memory, battery, or answer quality on ThoxMini, ThoxAir, ThoxClip, or ThoxKey hardware. Hardware qualification is a separate claim with no evidence in this program to date.
  2. The gate measures factuality against one facts package, not general capability. GATE49's 49 questions derive from facts card v1.1.0. A high score says the model states that card's facts, declines what the card leaves unpublished, and refuses the card's known-false claims. It says nothing about reasoning, coding, conversation quality, or any fact outside the card — and the probe's arithmetic result shows a model can tie the fleet's best gate score while regressing on a general task the gate never tests.
  3. Publication state at close. The two promoted builds (Air Wave C.2, Edge Wave C) and the shipped Mini baseline build are merged, GGUF-converted, endpoint-served, and Ollama-published, with the Ollama names verified registry-side by layer digest (§9.4, §9.5); for those slots the merged repository and its card are the servable artifact, not the adapter repository. The seven held adapters remain unmerged LoRA adapters in their candidate repositories, and the Clip slot's shipped artifact is the prior published build, which this program did not produce. No adapter or merged build in this program has been run on a device.
  4. Single-run measurements. Each gate result is one greedy pass by one job, identified by job id. The design makes re-runs near-deterministic, but no variance estimate across seeds, samplings, or prompt perturbations exists, and small score differences (one or two questions) should not be over-read — the rulings in this wave rest on hard failures and probe behaviour, not on the 43-vs-47 margin alone, with the recipe comparison in Section 8.5 explicitly confounded by backend and loss-masking differences.
  5. The corpus and the gate share a source. Both derive from the facts card, by design: the gate measures card-learning, and a model could in principle score well by memorizing decline shapes rather than facts. The borderline Air headcount failure shows the detector's shape-sensitivity cutting the other way. For the fix cycles the point is stronger than "in principle": the C.1 and C.2 corpus revisions were written from gate and probe failures, so those scores are development-set measurements (§7.3), and the null policy (§7.1) bounds what the instrument can certify. An independent question set, authored away from the corpus, is the known remedy and has not been built.
  6. Small-model ceilings are real. The Air model's verified-category recall (8/12) reflects a 0.5B model's capacity; the program's answer is mesh escalation to a larger tier, which is a system property this paper does not evaluate.
  7. Vendor-reported figures appear in the survey only. Challenger capability claims in Section 3 are labeled vendor-reported where they occur and were never used as THOX results; the slate verdicts rest on fleet evidence and structural properties (license, architecture, generation), but a reader should not carry any vendor number out of this paper as a measurement.
  8. Costs are modeled, not metered. Section 5.3's figures are computed from recorded runtimes and published flavor rates; the program did not reconcile them against the account's billing record for this paper.
  9. The gate's decline detector is form-sensitive. In Wave C.2, six hard failures across the Air and Mini results were charged against short decline forms the program itself had trained, which the detector did not recognize as declines; no false fact was stated in any of them (§9.3). The scores are reported as measured, unadjusted — but until the detector recognizes the canonical short-decline forms, the gate will keep charging models for the scorer's vocabulary gap, and cross-cycle comparisons at the one-or-two-question level inherit that noise.
  10. Merged is not served. Until this edition, no shipped artifact had been gated as served. Section 8.6 now measures the served path, and the gaps it found (Edge 16/49 as served against 46/49 merged; Clip 12/49 pre-fix against a 25/49 grounded base) are part of the record. The served numbers inherit every limitation above, plus one of their own: they were measured on a CPU-only cloud host through Ollama 0.40.13, not on device hardware or a deployment build, and against Modelfiles carrying the pre-correction grounding text (§8.6 sequencing note).
  11. Statistics. Every comparison in this paper rests on single runs of 49 paired items. On 49 items, a four-question difference with all discordant items in one direction gives an exact McNemar p of 0.125; the Wilson 95% interval for 43/49 spans roughly 37–46 questions and for 47/49 roughly 42–48. Score differences of one to four questions are therefore ordering evidence at best, and the rulings that matter rest on hard-failure classes and probe behaviour, not on those margins. No training-seed variance exists in the record: the registry entries record no seed, and no run was repeated under a second seed.
  12. Authorship and adjudication. The author of this paper is also the officer who set the bars, supervised the corpus fixes, and ruled on every result (front-matter disclosure). The checks on that conflict in this program were procedural — bars registered in advance, rulings and failures printed on the cards, and this post-publication review process — not an independent human review, which did not occur.

11Conclusion

Wave C replaced an accumulated model lineup with a slate and a standard, and the two fix cycles that followed tested whether the standard could also improve what it had judged. The slate held up: one defended flagship per device, chosen under a license policy that excluded an entire vendor line on principle, with the single switch (SmolLM2 in the role tier) made on structural grounds. The standard held up better, because it was willing to say no — in Wave C to three of four flagships, and in the fix cycles to five of six further adapters, including one that had passed its written bar. The program's closing state (§9.5) is two promoted flagships, one slot shipping its best measured build as a documented baseline with its caveat printed on its card, and one slot held at its prior published baseline because no candidate earned it.

The durable findings are not the scores. First, at this scale the behaviour skin is a corpus-and-recipe artifact: the same bases moved 19 → 46 across the corpus revision and 42/43 → 47 across the recipe change — both movements stated as measurements across confounded variables, not clean attributions: §8.5 records that the recipe gap is not an isolation of any single factor (measurement backend, loss masking, and step count also changed), and the Edge comparison likewise changed corpus, backend, and serving path together, so neither movement is credited to corpus alone or to recipe alone. Two of the worst failures in the program (a pricing answer, a published-models list) were located verbatim in the training data. Second, termination is a trainable behaviour distinct from knowledge: the C.1 models knew to decline and fabricated on continuation; the C.2 corpus taught stopping directly — short declines, continuation traps, verbatim-repeat multi-turn rows — and, with completion-only loss on the Mini stack, the pathology disappeared from every transcript. Third, the gate's strictness is the product: bars fixed before the runs, improvement read against the current candidate rather than a stale floor, a stopping rule that ships the best measured artifact rather than the newest, and a scorer whose own form-sensitivity is recorded as a limitation (§10) rather than adjusted away. What remains open is qualification, not training: no artifact has run on device hardware, the Mini baseline ships with a known tool-routing defect, the Clip slot awaits either a future cycle or a different base, and the Edge flagship — promoted on its merged-weights measurement — serves 16/49 on the content channel until a labelled think-policy configuration change is made and measured (§8.6). The measurements say what ships. This paper is their record.

12References

Related work. Four bodies of work bear directly on this program's design and findings, and this edition situates the paper against them. Gekhman et al. [20] show that fine-tuning on new knowledge is learned slowly and, as it is learned, linearly increases the model's tendency to hallucinate on its pre-existing knowledge — the mechanism behind this program's signature failure, fabrication surfacing inside otherwise correct declines. Ovadia et al. [21] find retrieval (in-context knowledge) beats fine-tuning for knowledge injection; §8.6's grounded-base runs are this paper's local measurement of the same comparison, and they set the bar the fine-tunes had to clear. R-Tuning [22] trains refusal on questions beyond the model's knowledge; GATE49's abstention and disclosure categories operationalize the same behaviour against a company's disclosure policy rather than a model's parametric knowledge. TruthfulQA [23] is the design ancestor of the known_false category (questions built on false presuppositions), and FActScore [24] represents the fine-grained atomic-fact evaluation family of which GATE49's trait scoring is a coarser, policy-bound relative.

15Publication and public documentation

The program's completion bar treated documentation as part of the deliverable: a model counts as done when it is trained, published, carries a card with its full training record, and is supported by a whitepaper and documentation package. This section records the public-documentation state that closed the program on October 30, 2026. It adds no results; every measurement in this paper stands as reported in Sections 8 and 9.

This paper. Version 0.3.0 of this paper was published on October 30, 2026 in the public Hugging Face dataset Thox-ai/thox-whitepapers, at https://huggingface.co/datasets/Thox-ai/thox-whitepapers/resolve/main/THOX_Wave_C_Flagship_Program_Whitepaper_v0.3.0.pdf, and verified by anonymous retrieval (HTTP 200; SHA-256 fbdf0c63cdc7f0e5476f8b5e3c16d431e05f6da97e87303af6b2786793d4efe0, matching the local build). Versions 0.4.0 and 0.4.1 were each published under their own filenames and, at the time, also replaced the content at the earlier versioned addresses for link stability. That practice was wrong for a paper whose subject is provenance, and it was reversed on October 30, 2026: the v0.3.0 address again serves the v0.3.0 edition (508,551 B, SHA-256 fbdf0c63cdc7f0e5476f8b5e3c16d431e05f6da97e87303af6b2786793d4efe0), the v0.4.0 address the v0.4.0 edition (513,921 B, SHA-256 e2cd91f9a67abd6eac84f240b57057c37a8ba43aa08b3e2bc3c07fcdcf8c8e94), and the v0.4.1 address the v0.4.1 edition (519,308 B, SHA-256 b1f77b3261e2ae6df03b3f8403fbb7df60dee75ebc4e933fc27ce9594f8e8bbf), each verified by anonymous download against the local builds. A separate alias, THOX_Wave_C_Flagship_Program_Whitepaper_latest.pdf, carries the current edition for link stability. This edition, v0.4.2, is published under its own filename and at the alias, and changes no earlier file. (The §14 row for v0.3.0 says "not submitted or published anywhere"; that described the draft's state when the row was written, before the October 30 publication, and §14's v0.4.0 row is the publication record.) The predecessor program paper, First Device Models, Trained In-House (Waves A–B, reference 1), was updated to a second edition on the same date, covering the final Wave B results, and is hosted in the same dataset.

Ollama model pages. The program's models are also published through Ollama under the Thox-ai namespace (ollama.com/Thox-ai). An inventory taken on October 30, 2026 counted 29 public model pages in the namespace; 15 of them carried no description and no readme at all, including every flagship push of October 29 — the weights had landed and the pages had not. On October 30, 2026 the flagship and edge model pages were rewritten to a single documentation standard and verified in place — the fleet's TXF-standard template: nine sections comprising a summary, the exact run commands and tags, intended use and device assignment, the model's GATE49 evaluation with its ruling, resources (the Hugging Face repository and this paper), limitations, and license and provenance, with badge images in the brand colour #05A451. The remaining pages in the namespace follow in the same pass, to the same template. The standard does not distinguish by outcome: a held adapter's page carries its held status and its failure record in the same form as a promoted model's page carries its promotion. The template and the inventory are program files (ollama-pages-20261030/TEMPLATE.md and INVENTORY.md).

License compliance on the distributed artifacts (read back 2026-10-30). Earlier editions' Track A language asserted more than the artifacts show. The accurate statement: THOX publishes its fine-tunes under the base models' licenses, with its own contribution offered on those same terms. Verified by read-back of every distributed repository named in this paper: the card metadata declares the base license in all sixteen, and none of the sixteen carries a LICENSE file or a NOTICE file — so the MIT notice obligation and the Apache-2.0 §4 license-copy and modification-notice obligations are not discharged inside the artifacts themselves. The gap is recorded here and in the review disposition; adding the files is a finishing-lane task and is not claimed as done in this edition.

Launch campaign. A public model-launch campaign announcing the models' availability was prepared — posts for X, LinkedIn, Instagram and Facebook, a Hugging Face announcement, a Kickstarter backer update, a short announcement video script, and graphics — and delivered to Craig Ross, Chief Executive Officer, for publication on October 30, 2026. Under the company's social process, publication is the CEO's step; this paper records the delivery, not the posting.

AAppendix A. Reproducibility (added in v0.4.2)

The gate package. The exact instrument that produced every GATE49 number in this paper is the vendored bundle in the supplement (wavec-supplement/gate49/): factuality_gate49.py (the fleet scorer, differing from its factory original by one REPO_ROOT line, recorded in the bundle's VENDOR.md), the facts package, the facts card v1.1.0 (facts/data/thox_facts.json, SHA-256 635d81ba119089328aca60bab11b5285347f0a73fa81cda686ff5328a8a163c9), grounding_system.txt (corrected version, 4,645 B, SHA-256 f4bd8a681a531cadea30a6a4e8853804ea3635ff5e965659f9aef3618fdeb54e; the probe runs and the shipped Modelfiles used the pre-correction 5,032 B version, SHA-256 fcd65985…, §8.6), run_gate49_job.py, and probe_flagship.py. The bundle is committed in both compute-plane repositories (canonical commit 8b46f482facf4a22902f6cddfbba125b1c1a12d8; mirror 064f5729818f0a9680de86108c528d62aa69f34b).

Decoding and seeds. Gate and probe generation is greedy, max 320 new tokens, weights-only house prompt for the gate and the grounding prompt for the probe. No training seed is recorded in any registry entry or job record in this program; runs are identified by job id. Exact re-execution would require re-derivation from the registry entries and profiles in the supplement; bit-exact reproduction is not claimed.

What the supplement does not contain. The training corpora themselves remain in the private dataset repository; their hashes, composition, changelogs, and row-class records are published (here and in the supplement manifest), and the gate package is complete — so every score in this paper can be re-derived against any candidate artifact, while re-running the training requires the private corpora. Wave A/B per-question gate outputs were not retained on the run hosts (recorded in that program's supplement) and cannot be reconstructed; all Wave C per-run reports exist and are included.
